mainTopic: Which מצוות apply outside ארץ ישראל: the exceptions of השמטת כספים and שילוח עבדים, and the argument over the 'הלכה' that forbids ערלה outside the Land.
overview: The amud opens with a rule: מצוות commanded before entering ארץ ישראל apply everywhere, and those commanded after entering apply only in the Land. The exceptions are השמטת כספים and שילוח עבדים. The גמרא asks why these two needed to be listed, since each is a חובת הגוף. For money-release, it answers that רבי links it to land-release, but only in time and not in place, because 'כי קרא שמטה לה׳' teaches that it applies everywhere. For freeing slaves, 'יובל היא' teaches that it applies everywhere. The word 'בארץ' teaches that it applies only when יובל is in force in the Land. Next comes a משנה: חדש is forbidden everywhere by the תורה, ערלה outside the Land by a 'הלכה', and כלאים by the סופרים. שמואל says that 'הלכה' means local practice, and רבי יוחנן says it means a הלכה למשה מסיני. עולא argues that his view explains why ספק ערלה is treated more strictly than ספק כלאים outside the Land, and he begins to challenge רב יהודה. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The general rule: מצוות before and after entering the Land
steps.stepSummary: A rule about where מצוות apply, based on when they were commanded, with two exceptions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any מצוה Israel was commanded before entering the Land applies both in the Land and outside it. A מצוה commanded after entering the Land applies only in the Land. The exceptions are cancelling debts and freeing slaves: even though they were commanded after entering the Land, they apply both in the Land and outside it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: when a מצוה was given decides where it applies. Two מצוות are listed as exceptions, and the next steps ask why they needed to be listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מצוות given in the מדבר are not tied to the Land, so they apply everywhere. מצוות given after entry are tied to the Land and apply only there. השמטת כספים and שילוח עבדים break this pattern and apply everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: cancelling of money debts in the שמיטה year
sending slaves free (in the יובל year)

phrases.english: Any מצוה that Israel was commanded
before their entry into the Land
applies both in the Land
and outside the Land.
A מצוה commanded after their entry into the Land
applies only in the Land,
except for the cancelling of money debts
and the freeing of slaves,
for even though they were commanded about them
after their entry into the Land

phrases.aramaic: נוֹהֶגֶת בֵּין בָּאָרֶץ בֵּין בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ.
phrases.english: they apply both in the Land and outside the Land.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מִצְוָה שֶׁנִּצְטַוּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל קוֹדֶם כְּנִיסָתָן לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section with the rule that will be analyzed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The timing of a מצוה's command decides where it applies, except that השמטת כספים and שילוח עבדים apply everywhere even though they were commanded after entry.

steps.title: Why list debt cancellation at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the need to list השמטת כספים as an exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: But cancelling debts is a personal obligation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why השמטת כספים needed to be listed. It is a duty on the person, not on the land, so of course it should apply everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חובת הגוף is a מצוה that depends on the person and not on the ground, like תפילין. Such מצוות normally apply everywhere anyway, so listing debt-release as a special exception seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: a personal obligation, not connected to the land

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not that the ruling is wrong. The גמרא agrees it applies everywhere and only asks why it had to be said.

phrases.english: The cancelling of money debts is a personal obligation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for one part of the rule in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: Listing השמטת כספים as an exception in step 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A personal obligation applies everywhere by default, so saying it applies outside the Land seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רבי's teaching links debt release to land release
steps.stepSummary: It had to be said because רבי ties money-release to land-release, which might make it look land-dependent.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed only because of what was taught in a ברייתא. רבי says: "And this is the matter of the release: he shall release." The פסוק speaks of two releases: one is the release of land, and one is the release of money. When you release land, you release money. When you do not release land, you do not release money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule had to be stated because of רבי's teaching, which links releasing money to releasing land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק puts the two releases together, money-release depends in some way on land-release. Once it is tied to the land, we might think it applies only in the Land, so the rule had to say it applies everywhere. רבי's own wording ties the link to time (בזמן), meaning whenever land-release is in force.
steps.whyThisMatters: According to רבי, when land-release is not practiced, money-release is not practiced either.

phrases.english: It was needed only for what was taught in a ברייתא.
As it was taught: רבי says:
"And this is the matter of the release: he shall release"
the פסוק is speaking about two releases:
one is the release of land,
and one is the release of money.
At a time when you release land,
you release money;
at a time when you do not release land,
you do not release money.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a hidden reason the ruling was needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since money-release is tied to land-release, one might think it applies only in the Land.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling teaches that even so, money-release applies outside the Land.

steps.title: Why not link it by place instead of time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the link to land-release could be about place, which would limit money-release to the Land.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: in a place where you release land, you release money, and in a place where you do not release land, you do not release money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on how רבי's link should be read. Maybe it means the same place, not the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land-release only happens in ארץ ישראל. If the link were about place, money-release would also apply only in the Land. That would contradict the ruling in step 1.

phrases.english: But say: in a place where you release land,
you release money,
and in a place where you do not release land,
you do not release money!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of רבי's link given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the link between the two releases as being about time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The link could just as well be about place, which would limit money-release to ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: The פסוק says debt release applies everywhere
steps.stepSummary: The words "כי קרא שמטה לה׳" teach that money-release applies in every place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "Because the release has been proclaimed for ה׳", meaning in every case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from another phrase in the same פסוק. It shows that money-release is not limited by place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "כי קרא שמטה לה׳" shows the release is proclaimed for ה׳, wherever a Jew is. So the link to land-release is only about time, not place. That is why money-release applies outside the Land too.
steps.whatToRemember: השמטת כספים is tied to land-release by time (רבי), but not by place. So it applies outside ארץ ישראל too, and this is the חידוש of the ruling in step 1.

phrases.english: The פסוק teaches:
"Because the release has been proclaimed for ה׳"
in every case.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר כִּי קָרָא שְׁמִטָּה לַה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 and ends this section.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Money-release might be limited to the place of land-release, ארץ ישראל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק says money-release applies everywhere; the link to land is only about time.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: השמטת כספים applies outside the Land, and this is what the ruling in step 1 comes to teach.

steps.title: Why say that freeing slaves applies everywhere?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the need to list שילוח עבדים as an exception, since it is a personal obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Freeing slaves is an obligation on the person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the second exception, freeing slaves, the same question it asked about money-release: why did this need to be said at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חובת הגוף is a מצוה on the person, not on the land. מצוות like that apply everywhere anyway. So listing שילוח עבדים as an exception seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: sending slaves free (in the יובל year)
an obligation on the person, not tied to the land

phrases.english: Freeing slaves is an obligation of the body!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge from step 2, now aimed at the second exception.
steps.kashyaTarget: Listing שילוח עבדים as an exception to the land rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A personal obligation applies everywhere anyway, so there is no need to say so.

steps.title: The words 'בארץ' could mislead, so 'יובל היא' teaches everywhere
steps.stepSummary: Without a teaching, 'בארץ' would suggest freeing slaves applies only in the Land. 'יובל היא' teaches that it applies in every place.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since it says 'proclaim liberty in the land,' it applies in the Land and not outside it. So the פסוק says 'it is a יובל' to teach that it applies in every place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the exception was needed because one word in the פסוק could make it look land-only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בארץ' could suggest the מצוה is limited to the Land. The extra words 'יובל היא' in the same פסוק show it applies everywhere. That is why it had to be listed.

keyTerms.meaning: it would enter your mind to say (a mistaken first thought)
therefore the פסוק says (to teach otherwise)

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say:
since it is written "And you shall proclaim liberty in the land,"
in the land, yes,
outside the land, no.
Therefore the verse says: "It is a Jubilee," meaning in every place.
phrases.notes: These words come from the same פסוק.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a reason it might have been mistaken for land-dependent, which a פסוק rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בארץ' limits freeing slaves to the Land
steps.terutzMaskana: 'יובל היא' teaches that it applies in every place

steps.title: Then why does the verse say 'in the land'?
steps.stepSummary: If freeing slaves applies everywhere, the word 'בארץ' needs an explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'in the land'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word 'בארץ' teaches, now that it does not limit the מצוה to the Land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה must teach something. The גמרא has just explained that 'בארץ' does not limit the place, so it needs to find a new job for that word.

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say "in the land"?

steps.title: Freedom outside the Land follows freedom in the Land
steps.stepSummary: 'בארץ' teaches that freeing slaves applies outside the Land only when it is in force in the Land.
steps.simpleTranslation: When freedom applies in the Land, it applies outside the Land. When it does not apply in the Land, it does not apply outside the Land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'בארץ' tells us when the מצוה is in force, not where it applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה depends on the Land in time, not in place. If יובל is in force in ארץ ישראל, slaves go free everywhere. If יובל is not in force there, slaves do not go free anywhere.
steps.whatToRemember: For שילוח עבדים: 'יובל היא' teaches that it applies in every place. 'בארץ' teaches that it depends on יובל being in force in the Land.
steps.confusionAlert: 'בארץ' here does not mean 'only in the Land.' It means 'only when it is in force in the Land.'

phrases.english: When the liberty applies in the Land,
phrases.notes: Freeing slaves happens in the יובל year, so this means a time when יובל is in force.

phrases.english: it applies outside the Land;
when the liberty does not apply in the Land,
it does not apply outside the Land.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בארץ' ties the מצוה to the time when liberty is in force in the Land

steps.title: A משנה: new grain, ערלה, and כלאים outside the Land
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that חדש is forbidden everywhere מן התורה, ערלה outside the Land is forbidden because of a 'הלכה', and כלאים outside the Land is forbidden by the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: new grain is forbidden by the תורה everywhere. ערלה is forbidden because of a 'הלכה'. כלאים is forbidden by the words of the סופרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source about land-related מצוות outside ארץ ישראל. This sets up a question about the word 'הלכה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three agricultural laws get three different levels outside the Land: Torah law, 'הלכה', and rabbinic law. The middle term, 'הלכה', is unclear. That is what the next steps discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: fruit of a tree in its first three years, which is forbidden

phrases.english: We learned there:

phrases.aramaic: הֶחָדָשׁ אָסוּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה בְּכׇל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: New grain is forbidden by Torah law in every place;
phrases.notes: This is grain from the new crop before the עומר offering.

phrases.english: ערלה is forbidden by a "halakha";
and כלאים is forbidden by the words of the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still about מצוות outside the Land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Outside the Land: חדש is forbidden by Torah law, ערלה by a 'הלכה', and כלאים by rabbinic law

steps.title: What does 'הלכה' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of 'הלכה' forbids ערלה outside the Land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word 'הלכה' in the משנה means. Two answers follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הלכה' could mean a law with real Torah-level authority, or just a custom. The answer decides how strict ערלה outside the Land is.

keyTerms.meaning: a law (here its meaning is unclear)

phrases.english: What is "halakha"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'הלכה' about ערלה outside the Land

steps.title: שמואל: it is the local practice
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל says the 'הלכה' is the law of the country, meaning a local practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: it is the law of the country.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: 'הלכה' here means a local custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, ערלה outside the Land is forbidden because it became the practice in those places. It is not a law given at Sinai.

keyTerms.meaning: the law of the country, a local practice

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
It is the law of the country.
phrases.notes: He means a practice that took hold in the places where Jews lived.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: it is a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.stepSummary: עולא in the name of רבי יוחנן says the 'הלכה' is a law given orally to משה at Sinai.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: it is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The second answer: 'הלכה' means an oral law from Sinai.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, ערלה outside the Land has the strength of a law from Sinai, not just a custom. This makes it much stronger than rabbinic כלאים.

keyTerms.meaning: an oral law given to משה at Sinai

phrases.english: Ulla said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is a halakha given to Moshe at Sinai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 11 that argues with step 12.

steps.title: עולא: my view explains why doubtful ערלה and doubtful כלאים differ
steps.stepSummary: עולא tells רב יהודה that his own view explains why a ספק of ערלה is treated differently from a ספק of כלאים. This sets up a challenge to שמואל's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to רב יהודה: It works out well for me, since I say it is a הלכה למשה מסיני. That is why we treat a doubt about ערלה differently from a doubt about כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא starts an argument against רב יהודה with 'בשלמא' ('it works for me...'). This prepares the challenge, 'but for you, what is the difference?', which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ערלה outside the Land comes from Sinai, it is stronger than rabbinic כלאים. That gives a reason why the two are treated differently when there is a doubt. If both are just custom or rabbinic, that difference is harder to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: it works out well according to me

steps.confusionAlert: A 'בשלמא' line is only the first half of a challenge. The real question against the other side comes in the next line.

phrases.english: Ulla said to Rav Yehuda:
It works out well according to me,
since I say it is a halakha given to Moshe at Sinai;
that is why we distinguish
between doubtful ערלה and doubtful כלאים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: עולא supports his view from step 13 and sets up an attack on step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that 'הלכה' means local practice
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only a Sinai-level ערלה explains why doubtful ערלה is treated differently from doubtful כלאים. The view of local practice seems to lose that difference.

steps.title: The משנה on uncertain ערלה
steps.stepSummary: עולא quotes a משנה: uncertain ערלה is forbidden in ארץ ישראל and permitted in סוריא. Outside the Land, a Jew may buy it from a non-Jew, as long as he does not see it being picked.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: fruit that might be ערלה is forbidden in ארץ ישראל and permitted in סוריא. Outside the Land, a Jew may go down to the non-Jew's field and buy the fruit, as long as he does not watch the non-Jew pick it.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא brings the first half of his proof. It is a משנה that sets the rules for fruit that might be ערלה. It is the first of two sources he will compare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside the Land, the Jew may only buy the uncertain fruit. He may not watch it being picked, because then the doubt would be gone and he would know it is ערלה. This rule is fairly strict. The next step shows that כלאים gets a looser rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit that might or might not be ערלה (fruit from a tree's first three years)
Syria, an area with an in-between status: not fully ארץ ישראל, not fully outside it
He goes down (into the field) and buys

phrases.english: As we learned: fruit that might be ערלה,
in the Land it is forbidden, in Syria it is permitted.
Outside the Land, he goes down and buys it,
as long as he does not see him picking it.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the non-Jewish owner. If the Jew saw him picking from a ערלה tree, it wouldn't be a doubt anymore.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind עולא's claim in Step 14 that his view explains a difference between ספק ערלה and ספק כלאים.
steps.raayaObject: That ערלה outside the Land has a stronger source than כלאים, as עולא says (הלכה למשה מסיני).
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה ערלה 3:9, the ruling on ספק ערלה

steps.title: The contrasting משנה on uncertain כלאים
steps.stepSummary: The same משנה rules on vegetables that might come from a vineyard with כלאים. They are forbidden in the Land and permitted in סוריא. Outside the Land, the Jew may buy them even while the non-Jew picks them in front of him, as long as the Jew does not pick them himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But about כלאים we learned: if a vineyard has vegetables planted in it, and vegetables are being sold outside it (and they might come from that vineyard), they are forbidden in ארץ ישראל and permitted in סוריא. Outside the Land, the produce may be picked (by the non-Jewish owner) and bought, as long as the Jew does not pick it by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא brings the second half of his proof, the rule for uncertain כלאים. He sets it next to the ערלה rule to show the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ספק ערלה outside the Land, the Jew may buy the fruit but may not even watch the non-Jew pick it. For ספק כלאים, the non-Jew may pick and the Jew may watch and buy. The only limit is that the Jew may not pick with his own hand. So ערלה is stricter. That makes sense if ערלה rests on a הלכה למשה מסיני and כלאים is only rabbinic, as the משנה from Step 10 says.

keyTerms.meaning: Whereas, but in contrast. It signals a comparison.
Forbidden mixtures. Here it means vegetables grown inside a vineyard.
A vineyard with vegetables planted in it

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the two similar words: in the ערלה rule it says לוֹקֵחַ (buys), and here it says לוֹקֵט (picks). For ערלה, the Jew may not even see the non-Jew picking. For כלאים, he may watch the picking. He just may not pick with his own hand.

phrases.english: Whereas regarding כלאים we learned:
a vineyard that has vegetables planted in it,
and vegetables are being sold outside it,
in the Land they are forbidden, in Syria they are permitted,
outside the Land, he goes down and picks.
phrases.notes: The non-Jewish owner does the picking here, and the Jew may stand and watch, unlike the ערלה case.

phrases.english: As long as he does not pick by hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second source for comparison, which shows that ספק כלאים is treated more leniently than the ספק ערלה of Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That ערלה and כלאים outside the Land come from different levels of source, so they are treated differently.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה ערלה 3:9, the ruling on ספק כלאים
steps.whyThisMatters: This difference is what עולא will use to challenge שמואל: if both were just local or rabbinic rules, why treat them differently?

steps.title: Turning the question on רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: עולא begins his challenge: 'But according to you…', meaning according to שמואל's view that the ערלה 'הלכה' is only a local practice.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. עולא is turning to רב יהודה to ask how his view (in the name of שמואל) can explain the difference just shown. The actual question continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under עולא's view, the difference is easy to explain: ערלה rests on Sinai, and כלאים is only rabbinic. Under שמואל's view, ערלה outside the Land is just a local custom. That is no stronger than a rabbinic rule, so the stricter treatment of ערלה looks hard to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: But, however. Here it turns the argument against the other side.
According to you, in your view

phrases.english: But according to you
phrases.notes: עולא is speaking to רב יהודה, so 'you' means the view he said in שמואל's name in Step 12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving that his own view explains the משנה, עולא now begins to show that רב יהודה's view in the name of שמואל cannot.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: the ערלה 'הלכה' is only a local practice (Step 12).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ערלה outside the Land is only a local practice, it should be no stricter than rabbinic כלאים. Yet the משנה treats ספק ערלה more strictly.
